decisions.reason: It remained on the website into 2024, so performance appears at least acceptable, but its weak fit with the firm’s transport-focused core makes it more vulnerable if aspirations are not met.
The service persisted through 2024 and is closer to the firm’s maritime labour and transport-related capabilities, so a large incumbent would likely continue it unless results clearly disappoint.
As a 2024 launch with its own page and six partner institutions already signed, it shows promising early traction and would likely be retained while the firm learns from the rollout.
The firm reports a concrete success in meeting the FuelEU deadline for all relevant vessels, indicating performance above a reasonable aspiration level in a growing regulatory market.
Although no standalone results are reported, the dashboard is integrated into the firm’s existing software and complements the successful compliance service, which supports keeping it on the market.

The simulation tool is also integrated into the firm’s software and fits the same regulatory solution bundle, so a large firm with some slack would likely continue it despite still-uncertain standalone demand.
